exposure: time interval between skin incision and delivery (S-D)
cohort: 426 mother-infant pairs who underwent emergency cesarean deliveries (ECD) for non-reassured fetal heart rate status over four years
finding: Longer S-D times were significantly associated with adverse neonatal outcomes, including lower 5th minute Apgar scores, increased NICU admissions, and higher neonatal death rates.
mod_finding: This study focused on emergency cesarean deliveries for fetal distress and found that while longer time between skin incision and delivery was associated with adverse neonatal outcomes, factors like previous cesarean delivery or maternal obesity may not directly impact those outcomes.
